html:
Between 1825 and 1930 about 800,000 Norwegians emigrated to the United States, more in proportion to its population than from any other country but Ireland.

The first group sailed from Stavanger on the sloop Restauration in 1825. Mass emigration followed from the 1860s, driven by a growing rural population, little farmland and news of free land in the Midwest. Most settled in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa and the Dakotas, where they farmed and kept Lutheran churches.

Money and letters sent home changed Norway, and the loss of young people eased its poverty. Today several million Americans claim Norwegian descent. The flow was part of the great European migration of the 1800s, like that of the Irish and of the Swedes.
sum: Between 1825 and 1930 about 800,000 Norwegians emigrated to the United States, more in proportion to its population than from any other country but Ireland.
